name: Fall Proof
tagline: Make your home and habits fall-proof after 60
about: Fall Proof audits your home room by room from photos, checks the medicines, footwear and lighting that quietly raise fall risk, and gives you a rehearsed plan for the night-time trip and for the fall itself.
persona: You are an occupational therapist specialising in falls prevention: practical, respectful of independence, precise about cheap fixes first.

onboarding.title: Most falls are preventable
onboarding.subtitle: A few details let us tailor the audit.
bullets: A rehearsed plan for if you fall

tools.title: Scan a room
tools.subtitle: Photo → hazards and fixes

inputs.label: Photo of a room, hallway, stairs or bathroom

tools.prompt: Inspect the room photo for fall hazards (rugs, cords, lighting, clutter, thresholds, grab points, furniture height, wet floors). Sections: a table (Hazard | Where | Risk level | Fix | Approx. cost), a checklist of free fixes to do today, and a callout on the single highest-risk item.

tools.title: Whole-home audit
tools.subtitle: Room-by-room checklist, cheapest first

inputs.label: Already fitted
inputs.placeholder: grab rail by the toilet, night light on the landing

tools.prompt: Build a falls audit for the profile's home covering {rooms}, skipping anything already fitted: {done}. Sections: a checklist per room of what to check and fix, ordered cheapest first, a table (Fix | Cost band | Who can fit it | Priority), bullets on grants, occupational-therapy referrals and equipment services that often exist for older residents, and a callout on the three fixes with the strongest evidence (lighting, rails, removing loose rugs).

tools.title: Medicines & dizziness
tools.subtitle: Which ones raise fall risk

inputs.label: Medicines and supplements
inputs.placeholder: amlodipine, zopiclone, codeine for the knee

tools.prompt: Review these medicines for the profile as general information only: {meds}; dizziness on standing: {dizzy}. Sections: a table (Medicine | Class | Fall-related effect to be aware of | Ask the pharmacist about), bullets of the questions to raise at a medication review (timing, dose, alternatives, standing slowly), steps for a safe stand-up routine (sit on the edge, count to ten, hold something, then go), and a callout that no medicine should be stopped or changed without the prescriber.

tools.title: Night-time plan
tools.subtitle: Safer trips to the bathroom
tools.prompt: Plan safe night-time trips for the profile ({trips} per night, route: {route}). Sections: steps for the trip itself (wake fully, sit, light on, footwear, hold the rail), a checklist of setup (motion-sensor lights, cleared path, bedside items, a commode or bottle if appropriate), a kv of evening habits that reduce trips (fluid timing, caffeine, alcohol, legs up in the afternoon), and a callout on when frequent night-time urination is worth mentioning to a doctor.

tools.title: If I fall
tools.subtitle: Getting up safely, and the plan
tools.prompt: Coach the profile through '{situation}'. Sections: steps for the safe sequence (check for injury, roll, crawl to a sturdy chair, kneel, rise) with one cue per step, bullets on what to do if you cannot get up (warmth, moving joints, calling for help), a checklist of preparation (phone placement, alarm pendant, keys with a neighbour), and a callout on injuries that mean stay put and call emergency services.

disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Never stop or change a medicine without the prescriber, and see a doctor after any fall with injury, blackout or new dizziness.
